body:
Here's some results from my investigation into the issue.

# The Main Problem

The basic setup required is to have multiple scenes (let's call them "A.tscn", "B.tscn", etc) which all reference a shared external resource. A `VisualShader` is an ideal one, as it loads many internal resources which seems to increase the chance of the crash, but I think any resource would exhibit the problem.

We call `load_threaded_request` to load "A.tscn" and "B.tscn".  At some point, these calls end up loading the shared `VisualShader`, and race on the loading. But the actual cause of the race is quite subtle. Here is an example scenario:

 - A begins loading the `VisualShader` on one thread, but gets paused (OS interrupts it or whatever).
 - B begins loading the `VisualShader` on another thread.
 - Since it sees that there's a load task for this asset already, it enters `WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion`.
 - The "Deadlock prevention" branch of the code triggers, because the first load task is older. This causes the "B" load to begin another load task for the same asset.
 - At some point, the "A" load unpauses. Now both loads are racing to load the same asset, causing unpredictable thread timing issues.

To be honest, I haven't completely figured out exactly what in the `VisualShader` `_set` code is non-thread-safe. However, it seems pretty clear-cut to me that not every object would have a thread-safe API, and so the racing load could probably cause all sorts of unpredictable issues. Doing a brief search, I already found a couple issues that are likely related, but mention resources other than `VisualShader`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111202
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115069

# Deadlock Prevention

So what's the deadlock prevention branch for anyway? In the basic scenario I describe above, it seems like we could skip the deadlock prevention branch entirely, and allow B.tscn's load of the `VisualShader` to wait on A.tscn's load. All would be good.

Unfortunately, simply removing this branch causes other, more subtle bugs. For example, the following can occur:

 - A.tscn depends on B.tscn. C.tscn depends on A.tscn.
 - We start loading A on one thread, and then start loading B on another.
 - The load for B takes a long time.
 - The A thread sees that its dependency B is loading right now, so it awaits on it.
 - This await causes the A worker thread to look for new work. It sees that C is available to load, so it begins loading it.
 - Oops - C depends on A, which we are loading further up the stack.

It seems the deadlock prevention branch is built to fix this issue, where there is no way to free up A for C without unwinding the stack all the way back up. This makes sense, and yet...

# What's the way out?

Clearly the deadlock prevention code is necessary, but as shown in the first section, it causes race conditions in certain scenarios.

Unfortunately, I still don't have an answer here. One route forward is to ensure that all operations called by all loading operations are threadsafe. That seems quite unfeasible (though I will probably be mitigating the problem in our main project by trying to do this just for `VisualShader`). Is there perhaps another route that allows us to fix the problem in `WorkerThreadPool` itself? I'm unsure, and I could use some help finding a real solution.
I have a machine with a similarly high number of cores, I'll have a look at it tomorrow. No promises, but if I can repro it I should be able to fix it.
To help me tomorrow, do you have any information on crash frequency, platform, or any other details? I'm on the Godot rocket.chat as well, (`@hp`) feel free to ping me there.
I don't have much more detail than I've posted, but I've started a thread on RocketChat: https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/core?msg=ex5iJaCcCsLAQFmP5

After a few more hours investigation, I think I have a general idea of what's going on with `VisualShader` specifically.

 - The first thread that makes it in calls `set_path` on the `VisualShader` in `_run_load_task`. This puts the shader into the `ResourceCache`.
 - Later, the thread begins setting properties on this `VisualShader` object.
 - At some point, another thread calls `_run_load_task` too, because of the deadlock prevention code described above.
 - If it manages to out-pace the first loading thread, then it will pull the `VisualShader` out of the cache, and also begin setting properties on it.
 - Both threads are now calling `set` on various properties in the `VisualShader`. The problematic one, for us, seems always to be `nodes/fragments/connections`, which generates a connection between two nodes.
 - If both threads happen to enter the `HashMap._insert` function around the same time, then the following can happen:
    - One thread allocates `hashes` and `elements`, then inserts an element.
    - The other thread, still stuck at the top of `_insert`, begins running. It also allocates `hashes` and `elements`, overwriting the first thread's allocation.
 - Then, the first thread (or even a third thread) does an index into the same `HashMap`. It sees that `num_elements` is nonzero, and tries to access some data in `elements`, which is empty.

The upshot of this is that `HashMap` is not at all threadsafe. A spot-fix for `VisualShader` would be to use some threadsafe container in `_set` and defer to the main thread for real initialization.

I think the main problem is that the deadlock prevention can't tell the difference between a nested load and simultaneous loads. 

In the MRP multiple threads try to load 16 tscn files. Each of the tscn files depend on `res:://vfx/decimillipede_suck_shader.tres` 

If all threads load then the 16 "unique" tscn files start loading, and they all stage `res:://vfx/decimillipede_suck_shader.tres`  for loading. Because there are no dependencies the first one starts off and starts loading the shader. 

The other 15 threads then see that there is already a Task to load `res:://vfx/decimillipede_suck_shader.tres`  and wrongly assume that it is being loaded as a deeper dependency. But what is actually happening is that it is already being loaded. In order to "break the deadlock" all threads then immediately try to load `res:://vfx/decimillipede_suck_shader.tres` as well.

At this point there are 16 threads all trying to load the same resource.
